Countdown target matches the banner published at keepandroidopen.org. The app updates once per second while it is open.
ANDROID IS NOW A LOCKED-DOWN PLATFORM
ANDROID BECOMES A LOCKED-DOWN PLATFORM IN
The “advanced flow” is not a solution

Android Developer Verification is a Google program that links every app to a verified developer identity before it can be installed on certified Android devices. Developers must verify who they are and register the package names they publish. Apps without a registered, verified developer can no longer be installed the normal way once the protections roll out.

It lands hardest on independent and open-source distribution such as F-Droid, direct APK downloads, and hobby projects. Google says it is about safety and stopping anonymous malware. Critics including the Keep Android Open campaign, F-Droid and the EFF say it is a gatekeeper kill switch: central registration, government ID, a fee, and full control over what your device is allowed to trust.

The advanced flow is delivered through Google Play services, not the Android OS, so Google can change, restrict or remove it at any time without an OS update or user consent. The 24-hour delay is intentionally disruptive and is one more step that stands between you and software you choose to run.

string-array.name: timeline_titles
string-array.item: Android Developer Verifier ships to devices
Global console, limited accounts, advanced flow

string-array.name: timeline_details
string-array.item: Google announces that beginning in 2027, apps for Android must be registered to a verified developer, including apps installed outside Google Play.
Power users get a deliberately cumbersome escape hatch: enable Developer Options, confirm you are not being coerced, restart, then wait 24 hours before you may allow unverified installs.
A background system service (com.google.android.verifier) is pushed through Google System Updates to certified devices and stays dormant until enforcement.
Google confirms enforcement starts September 30, 2026, across seven stores and four countries.
The Android Developer ID Status API launches globally and early access begins for the Android Developer Console API and limited distribution accounts.
Limited distribution accounts (free, up to 20 devices, no government ID) and the Console API launch worldwide. The advanced flow for unverified sideloading begins rolling out.

Protections go live for users in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand on certified devices running Android 7+. Apps from unverified developers are blocked on the participating stores: Google Play, HONOR App Market, OPPO App Market, Galaxy Store, Palm Store, V-Appstore and GetApps.
Verification is expanded to all apps and regions. Keep Android Open counts down to January 1, 2027, when Android becomes a locked-down platform.

resources.string: Act now — make your voice heard

Regulators want to hear from individuals who are affected. Be polite and specific, write in an official language of the body you contact, ask for a written acknowledgement, and copy %1$s so the campaign can track victories.
The Department of Justice and the FTC take antitrust reports through online forms. Use them, and contact your own representative and senators directly.

resources.string: Stop Google\'s Android Developer Verification lockdown

Dear %1$s representative,

I am writing as a concerned Android user and as a citizen in your jurisdiction.

Google's Android Developer Verification program, enforced starting September 30, 2026 in several markets and expanding globally in 2027, will require every Android app to be registered to a centrally verified developer before it can be installed on certified devices. Developers must submit government identification, agree to Google's terms, pay a fee and list every current and future app identifier.

This does not meaningfully improve security. It hands a single private company the power to decide which software people are allowed to run on the devices they own, and it threatens independent and open-source distribution such as F-Droid, which cannot comply and may cease to exist.

I respectfully ask that you:

1. Investigate whether this program is anti-competitive and constitutes an abuse of a gatekeeper position.
2. Press Google to exempt open-source and non-commercial distribution, and to keep sideloading free of centralized registration.
3. Protect the right of users to run software of their choosing on hardware they purchased.

Please acknowledge this message in writing and let me know what action your office takes.

I am also copying the Keep Android Open campaign at %2$s.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your city and country]
